To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the intersection of 2 halfspaces on {ie73-3}n has threshold-degree {ie73-4}, that this is the first non-trivial lower bound for the threshold degree of any Boolean function, and that this implies that the intersection of halfspaces is hard to learn in the PAC model.
the intersection of 2 halfspaces on {ie73-1}n has degree {ie73-4}n, and that the intersection of {ie73-5} halfspaces on {e73-6}n has degree at least {ie73-7}n.
the threshold degree of the intersection of two {ie73-1} halfspaces is {ie73-3} and the threshold degree of a {ie73-4} DNF formula is {ie73+5}.
In summary, our research is concerned with
two questions: 1) How large is the threshold degree of the intersection of two linear functions on {0, 1}n?
the following two questions: (1) Can a function f:Rn → R be sign-represented by polynomials of degree O(1)?
the complexity of sign-representation of Boolean functions, which is closely related to the computational complexity of Boolean formulas, and has important applications in learning theory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the threshold degree of a Boolean function is the most difficult parameter to be estimated.
the complexity of learning DNF formulas, read-once Boolean functions, intersection of two half-spaces, and parity is respectively {ie73-3}, Ω(n), Ω(n), and Ω(n).
the intersection of halfspaces on {ie73-1} is not learnable from sign-representing polynomials, while the intersection of halfspace on {ie73-n} is learnable from sign representing polynomials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the intersection of halfspaces on {ie73-4}n can be efficiently learned, but not sign-represented, by polynomials of low degree.
the intersection of any two halfspaces on n variables can be computed by a polynomial-size circuit of depth O(logn) but not by a polynomial-size threshold circuit of constant depth.

the intersection of halfspaces is not learnable in {ie73-3} time by a polynomial threshold function learner, while DNF formulas are learnable in {e73-3} and read-once formulas are learnable even in {ie73+1} time by a threshold function learner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the complexity of the intersection of two Boolean functions may depend on the complexity of the functions individually, and the complexity of a function may depend on the functions it intersects.
the intersection of halfspaces is not learnable by a polynomial-size DNF formula.
the threshold degree of a Boolean function is not necessarily related to its learnability.
